key_insight: A proactive integrated care model for people with complex needs was hard to test because far fewer patients than expected qualified or enrolled, but it still improved coordination with social work and was seen as useful by practices.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest that matching eligibility rules and recruitment to the local care context is crucial when designing integrated care programs for patients with complex, multi-domain needs.
method: Mixed-method process evaluation using the RE-AIM framework
Used questionnaires, routine care data, and semi-structured interviews
Analyzed quantitative data descriptively and interviews thematically
evidence_signal: Only 153 of 1403 screened patients were eligible and 30 enrolled, limiting conclusions on effectiveness, while process data showed improved collaboration and broad practice uptake.
watch_item: The main implementation concern was very low enrollment due to a restrictive inclusion process and low acute-care use, which limited assessment of cost-effectiveness and outcomes.
paper_title: Lessons learned from a trial on integrated and proactive care for patients with complex needs (Hotspotters project): a process evaluation
